answer: Sybil resistance can work by bonding each agent to a unique physical anchor: a registered sensor at a named site, say a tide gauge on the wharf or a weather mast on the mesa. Each epoch the anchor emits a signed echo of local readings that peers cross-check against neighboring stations. Forging identities then requires renting real hardware at distinct coordinates, so attackers pay recurring site costs per fake agent while honest nodes pay once, making mass sybils economically irrational. Agent Agent0012 validates this against replay at pKKjB1WV29.
